{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_d4fd104b9cb24bccaaade76a","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\tThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n9\t\n10\t`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n11\t\n12\tRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n17\t\n18\t## Acceptance criteria\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n21\t- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n22\t- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n23\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n24\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n25\t\n26\t## Tech notes\n27\t\n28\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n29\t\n30\tOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n31\t\n32\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8c486030-8952-472b-9334-4205ae977544","uuid":"276b037a-a8e4-422e-8fd5-dde6e1a8c56c","timestamp":"2026-10-30T17:53:48.170Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/db6f74a2c8a2/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\nLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\nThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n\n`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n\nRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n\n## What to do\n\nCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n\n## Tech notes\n\nKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n\n","numLines":32,"startLine":1,"totalLines":32}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_d4fd104b9cb24bccaaade76a","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_97b549bfd5944f73b7b022b7","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Definition of Done\n2\t\n3\t> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n4\t\n5\t**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.\n6\t\n7\t## Done when these pass\n8\t\n9\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n10\t      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n11\t\n12\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n13\t      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n14\t\n15\t## Facets\n16\t\n17\t- [x] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.\n18\t- [x] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.\n19\t- [x] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.\n20\t\n21\t## Out of scope\n22\t\n23\t- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).\n24\t- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).\n25\t- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).\n26\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8c486030-8952-472b-9334-4205ae977544","uuid":"b1d90aee-6d5b-4786-800e-c580d919cf25","timestamp":"2026-10-30T17:53:50.589Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/db6f74a2c8a2/workspace/target/.lore/dod.md","content":"# Definition of Done\n\n> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n\n**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.\n\n## Done when these pass\n\n- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n## Facets\n\n- [x] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.\n- [x] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.\n- [x] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).\n- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).\n- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).\n","numLines":26,"startLine":1,"totalLines":26}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_97b549bfd5944f73b7b022b7","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

error.message : String(error);\n341\t    log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});\n342\t  }\n343\t}\n344\t\n345\t// onError is typed against Error and must not miss a class of failure, so a caught non-Error is wrapped and the original kept as cause.\n346\tfunction asError(rejection: unknown): Error {\n347\t  if (rejection instanceof Error) return rejection;\n348\t  return new Error(describeRejection(rejection), {cause: rejection});\n349\t}\n350\t\n351\t// The wrapped message is the thrown string itself, JSON for an object, and String() for a value neither handles.\n352\tfunction describeRejection(rejection: unknown): string {\n353\t  if (typeof rejection === 'string') return rejection;\n354\t  try {\n355\t    const json = JSON.stringify(rejection);\n356\t    if (json !== undefined) return json;\n357\t  } catch {\n358\t    // Unserializable values describe themselves instead.\n359\t  }\n360\t  return String(rejection);\n361\t}\n362\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8c486030-8952-472b-9334-4205ae977544","uuid":"ec5c3c33-5755-49f9-94e6-65404a4bb1e1","timestamp":"2026-10-30T17:54:55.297Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/db6f74a2c8a2/workspace/target/src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts","content":"  };\n}\n\n// A store outage is not a reason to fail the turn the customer already received.\nasync function saveSession(store: SessionStore | undefined, session: ChatSession): Promise<void> {\n  if (!store?.save) return;\n\n  try {\n    await store.save(session);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});\n  }\n}\n\n// onError is typed against Error and must not miss a class of failure, so a caught non-Error is wrapped and the original kept as cause.\nfunction asError(rejection: unknown): Error {\n  if (rejection instanceof Error) return rejection;\n  return new Error(describeRejection(rejection), {cause: rejection});\n}\n\n// The wrapped message is the thrown string itself, JSON for an object, and String() for a value neither handles.\nfunction describeRejection(rejection: unknown): string {\n  if (typeof rejection === 'string') return rejection;\n  try {\n    const json = JSON.stringify(rejection);\n    if (json !== undefined) return json;\n  } catch {\n    // Unserializable values describe themselves instead.\n  }\n  return String(rejection);\n}\n","numLines":33,"startLine":330,"totalLines":362}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_c1a615c3a5f343e7b24a645a","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2da18ceeb5224c73baba7a2b","type":"tool_result","content":"12:- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n13:- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n14:- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n15:- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n16:- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n17:- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n18:- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n19:- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n23:- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n---\ndiff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md\nindex eab0af2..1c68cb0 100644\n--- a/CHANGELOG.md\n+++ b/CHANGELOG.md\n@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@ package, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.\n ### Fixed\n \n - `onError` and `afterSession` hooks now fire when `beforeSession` throws, matching the guarantee the hook names imply. Previously, a throw from `beforeSession` escaped the `try`/`finally` block entirely, so neither hook ran. **Migration note**: if your `afterSession` hook assumed it would only be called after a full session turn, it will now also be called when `beforeSession` itself fails — the hook can inspect the session to detect this case (no entries beyond the initial user message will have been processed).\n+- `onError` now fires for every rejection inside a turn, not only for rejections that are `Error` instances. Previously the orchestrator's `catch` gated the hook on `error instanceof Error`, so a provider rejecting with a string, a plain object, or `undefined` bypassed the hook entirely while the caller still saw the rejection — a hook counting failures, paging, or writing incident records read \"no errors\" for exactly those turns. The hook now receives an `Error` whose `message` describes the value (the thrown string itself, JSON for an object) and whose `cause` holds the original value, so a hook that wants the raw rejection can still reach it. **Migration note**: the value your caller receives is unchanged — only what `onError` sees is new; A link whose fragment is not a line number is not an anchor and is left alone, however much the file around it moves ([validated by: leaves a link whose fragment is not a line number untouched](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L506)). Test files are the common case, but nothing restricts it to them: a citation into a workflow, a config or a script is repointed the same way ([validated by: repoints docs, README and script citations alike](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L454), [root config](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L476), [workflow and manifest](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L490)).\n\nThe label is not part of the anchor. A descriptive label such as `[validated by]` is never touched ([validated by: leaves a descriptive label alone while syncing a short-form one beside it](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L420)). A short-form `[Lnn](../../src/X.test.ts#Lnn)` is different: its label carries no meaning beyond the number, so it is force-synced to whatever its own href says ([validated by: syncs labels even in a spec skipped for a differing anchor set](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L399)). Syncing happens after the rewrite, so a repointed href carries its label with it in the same run ([validated by: carries the label along when the href is repointed](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L354)).\n\n## The baseline is the point\n\nBaseline line numbers come from the base ref's copy of the **spec**, never from the working copy.\n\n- That is what makes a second run against the same baseline a no-op rather than a second translation ([validated by: is a no-op the second time, because the baseline is read from the base ref](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L76)).\n- `base-ref` defaults to `origin/main` ([validated by: defaults the base ref to origin/main](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L612)).\n\nThree cases have no baseline to reason from, and each is skipped rather than guessed:\n\n- A spec absent from the base ref is skipped whole. A red check is fixed by running the script without `--check` and committing what it rewrote.\n\nThe gate has a blind spot worth knowing. Specs that do not exist on `origin/main` yet — every spec on the branch that introduced them — are skipped for the baseline comparison, so on such a branch only the rotten check is really running. Staleness in a new spec is caught from the first merge onward, not before.\n\n## Recorded decisions\n\n- **A tie is a failure, not a guess.** The resolver could pick the first candidate, or the nearest to the old line. Both are plausible and both are silently wrong some of the time, which is the exact failure this script exists to prevent. Reporting ambiguity costs a person one decision and never moves a citation to the wrong place.\n- **Rotten is checked without a baseline.** It would be simpler to check anchors only where a baseline exists, but that is precisely where new specs are, and a brand-new citation onto a closing brace is as broken as an old one.\n- **Labels are force-synced, hrefs are not.** A retargeted href is a deliberate edit and is preserved. A short-form label that disagrees with it is not a deliberate edit — it is a leftover — so it is overwritten rather than reported.\n- **A tie is reported, not broken, and the suite says so.** `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts` drives the script against throwaway git repositories, because the whole subject is a base ref against a working tree. That failure mode is a review concern, and the `require-spec-link` backlog is the instrument that surfaces it: the test the citation should have named goes on reading as uncited.\n\n## The script's contract\n\n`node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs [--check] [base-ref]`\n\n- A plain run rewrites stale anchors in place and syncs short-form labels to their hrefs ([validated by: syncs a label to the line its own href names](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L341)).\n- `--check` rewrites nothing. It reports stale anchors instead, and reports a label disagreeing with its href as `mislabelled` ([validated by: --check names a label disagreeing with its href and rewrites nothing](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L367)).\n- Because `--check` judges labels against their current, un-repointed hrefs, a stale href is reported as stale in check mode and its label follows once a plain run repoints it. The two runs still converge in one pass ([validated by: converges: after one plain run, check passes and a second run is a no-op](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L382)).\n- Both modes print one summary line: the counts of moved-or-stale, up to date, unresolved, and relabelled-or-mislabelled anchors, plus a `retargeted (not checked)` line when that count is above zero.\n- Details go to stderr, each prefixed with its kind: `stale`, `unresolved`, `rotten`, `mislabelled` ([validated by: exits 1 listing stale anchors and rewrites nothing](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L111)).\n- An anchor resting on the `describe` that groups a test is accepted: a statement can be validated by a whole group ([validated by: accepts an anchor on the describe line](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L542)).\n- A citation into a file outside `src/` — a root config, a workflow — is repointed like any other ([validated by: repoints a citation into a root config file](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L476)).\n\nExit codes:\n\n- `0` — nothing to fix ([validated by: exits 0 once a plain run has repointed them](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L130)).\n- `1` — any rotten or unresolved anchor, in either mode; and in `--check`, any stale or mislabelled one ([validated by: does not report one the rewrite itself repoints](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L308)).\n- `2` — an unrecognised flag. Nothing is scanned ([validated by: exits 2 with usage on an unknown flag](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L640)).\n- `2` — more than one base ref ([validated by: exits 2 with usage on more than one base ref](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L644)).\n- `2` — a base ref that does not resolve to a commit ([validated by: exits 2 naming a base ref that does not resolve](../../scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts#L631)).\n\n## CI\n\n`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main` as the `Spec anchor check` step, and the workflow checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` because a shallow clone cannot serve `origin/main`. A red check is fixed by running the script without `--check` and committing what it rewrote.\n\nThe gate has a blind spot worth knowing. Specs that do not exist on `origin/main` yet — every spec on the branch that introduced them — are skipped for the baseline comparison, so on such a branch only the rotten check is really running. Staleness in a new spec is caught from the first merge onward, not before.\n\n## Recorded decisions\n\n- **A tie is a failure, not a guess.** The resolver could pick the first candidate, or the nearest to the old line. Both are plausible and both are silently wrong some of the time, which is the exact failure this script exists to prevent. Reporting ambiguity costs a person one decision and never moves a citation to the wrong place.\n- **Rotten is checked without a baseline.** It would be simpler to check anchors only where a baseline exists, but that is precisely where new specs are, and a brand-new citation onto a closing brace is as broken as an old one.\n- **Labels are force-synced, hrefs are not.** A retargeted href is a deliberate edit and is preserved. A short-form label that disagrees with it is not a deliberate edit — it is a leftover — so it is overwritten rather than reported.\n- **A tie is reported, not broken, and the suite says so.** `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.test.ts` drives the script against throwaway git repositories, because the whole subject is a base ref against a working tree. It is adapted from an existing suite for the same script, at one assertion per test.\n(eval):1: == not found","tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_b29a1f4778ab4d30985fa9a4","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{createChatOrchestrator} from './chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {OrchestratorHooks} from './chatOrchestrator.js';\nimport type {AIProvider, MessageChunk, SendMessageParams, UsageMetadata} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport {AIError} from '../types/ai.js';\nimport type {ChatSession} from '../types/session.js';\nimport {PromptBuilder} from '../infrastructure/builders/promptBuilder.js';\nimport {ToolRegistry} from './tools/registry.js';\nimport type {ToolResponse} from './tools/registry.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../types/messages.js';\nimport type {SessionEntry} from '../types/session.js';\n\n// Fixed: nothing asserts on it, and new Date() would tie the run to the clock.\nconst SENT_AT = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';\n\n// One expect per test needs the rejection as a value rather than a matcher.\nconst outcomeOf = (call: Promise<unknown>): Promise<string> =>\n  call.then(() => 'resolved without throwing').catch((error: Error) => error.message);\n\nfunction createSession(content: string): ChatSession {\n  return {\n    sessionId: 's1',\n    userId: 'u1',\n    entries: [{role: 'user', content, timestamp: SENT_AT}],\n  };\n}\n\nfunction createMockProvider(response: string, usage?: UsageMetadata): AIProvider {\n  return {\n    async *sendMessage(_params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      yield {type: 'text', text: response};\n      yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn', usage};\n    },\n    async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n      return {} as T;\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nfunction createErrorProvider(error: Error): AIProvider {\n  return {\n    // eslint-disable-next-line require-yield\n    async *sendMessage(): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      throw error;\n    },\n    async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n      return {} as T;\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nconst promptBuilder = new PromptBuilder({identity: 'You are a test assistant.'});\n\ntype RecordedHook =\n  | 'beforeSession'\n  | 'beforeUserInput'\n  | 'afterUserInput'\n  | 'beforeModelResponse'\n  | 'afterModelResponse'\n  | 'afterSession'\n  | 'onError';\n\n// Only the named hooks are installed: one that merely exists changes the observed order.\nconst recordingHooks = (callOrder: string[], names: RecordedHook[]): OrchestratorHooks => {\n  const all: Required<Pick<OrchestratorHooks, RecordedHook>> = {\n    beforeSession: async () => void callOrder.push('beforeSession'),\n    beforeUserInput: async (_session, msg) => {\n      callOrder.push('beforeUserInput');\n      return msg;\n    },\n    afterUserInput: async () => void callOrder.push('afterUserInput'),\n    beforeModelResponse: async (_session, systemPrompt) => {\n      callOrder.push('beforeModelResponse');\n      return systemPrompt;\n    },\n    afterModelResponse: async () => void callOrder.push('afterModelResponse'),\n    afterSession: async () => void callOrder.push('afterSession'),\n    onError: async () => void callOrder.push('onError'),\n  };\n\n  return Object.fromEntries(names.map(name => [name, all[name]])) as OrchestratorHooks;\n};\n\n// Records what the orchestrator actually sent, for tests that assert on the request.\nconst capturingProvider = (): {provider: AIProvider; sent: {systemPrompt: string; lastUserContent: string}} => {\n  const sent = {systemPrompt: '', lastUserContent: ''};\n\n  return {\n    sent,\n    provider: {\n      async *sendMessage(params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n        sent.systemPrompt = params.systemPrompt;\n        const last = params.messages[params.messages.length - 1];\n        sent.lastUserContent = typeof last.content === 'string' ? last.content : '';\n        yield {type: 'text', text: 'ok'};\n        yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: 'end_turn'};\n      },\n      async generateStructured<T>(): Promise<T> {\n        return {} as T;\n      },\n    },\n  };\n};\n\ndescribe('ChatOrchestrator hooks', () => {\n  describe('beforeSession', () => {\n    it('called before anything else', async () => {\n      const callOrder: string[] = [];\n      const hooks = recordingHooks(callOrder, ['beforeSession', 'beforeUserInput', 'beforeModelResponse']);\n\n      const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(createMockProvider('hi'), promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n      await orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('hello'));\n\n      expect(callOrder[0]).toBe('beforeSession');\n    });\n\n    it('runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller', async () => {\n      const callOrder: string[] = [];\n      let onErrorMessage: string | undefined;\n      const hooks: OrchestratorHooks = {\n        beforeSession: async () => {\n          callOrder.push('beforeSession');\n          throw new Error('beforeSession boom');\n        },\n        onError: async (_session, error) => {\n          callOrder.push('onError');\n          onErrorMessage = error.message;\n        },\n        afterSession: async () => {\n          callOrder.push('afterSession');\n        },\n      };\n\n      const orchestrator = createChatOrchestrator(createMockProvider('never'), promptBuilder, undefined, {hooks});\n      const outcome = await outcomeOf(orchestrator.processMessage(createSession('hello')));\n\n      expect({outcome, onErrorMessage, callOrder}).toEqual({\n        outcome: 'beforeSession boom',\n        onErrorMessage: 'beforeSession boom',\n        callOrder: ['beforeSession', 'onError', wrapped Error when the provider rejects with undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L311)).","originalFile":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":7,"newStart":16,"newLines":7,"lines":[" - This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string, a plain object, or `undefined` is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L64), [validated by: calls onError with a wrapped Error when the provider rejects with undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L311)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":7,"newStart":15,"newLines":7,"lines":[" - The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153))."," - A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L589)).\n- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string, a plain object, or `undefined` is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L64), [validated by: calls onError with a wrapped Error when the provider rejects with undefined](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L311)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error
